$comment: Checks that still race a click against page.waitForLoadState().
THE DEFECT. waitForLoadState() resolves against the document ALREADY ON
SCREEN, and that document is already loaded -- so
await Promise.all([
page.waitForLoadState('domcontentloaded').catch(() => {}),
control.click({ timeout }),
returns immediately, before the click's navigation has started. Whatever the
check reads next is the page's PREVIOUS state: a search validates the previous
result set, a saved form is read back before it was saved. Every one passes.
It resembles the documented Playwright idiom, which uses waitForNavigation --
that form waits for a NEW navigation and is correct; only the waitForLoadState
spelling is wrong, and only those are counted here.
THE FIX is clickAndAwaitReload() in scripts/lib/playwright-ui.js, which arms
the navigation wait before the click and fails when nothing navigates.
THIS FILE IS A BURN-DOWN, not a permission. playwright-navigation-race.test.js
fails the build when a file's count RISES or a new file appears, so the defect
cannot spread; lower a number when you migrate a call site, and delete the
entry at zero. It was measured, not chosen: these are the checks that already
had it when the shared helper was introduced, none of which can be verified
against a browser in the session that found them.
